SC-PUB-001.headline: Riverside had the slowest benefit processing last quarter at 26.3 business days.
SC-PUB-001.narrative: Business days from a complete application to decision, excluding applications on hold for documents (BR-PUB-002). South was fastest at 19.2 days across 4 districts; the county average was 21.4 days.

A.headline: North had the slowest benefit processing last quarter at 19.8 business days.

SC-PUB-002.headline: Including document holds, North had the slowest benefit processing last quarter at 31.0 business days.
SC-PUB-002.narrative: You asked to include applications on hold for documents, so BR-PUB-002 is not applied. North's new income-verification checklist put far more applications on hold — compare with the standard measure, which excludes them.

A.headline: Including document holds, North had the slowest benefit processing last quarter at 31.0 business days.

SC-PUB-003.headline: The timely processing rate is 89.2% this year — within the target band.
SC-PUB-003.narrative: Decided applications decided within 30 business days of a complete application, excluding applications on hold for documents (BR-PUB-002, BR-PUB-003).

SC-PUB-004.headline: Mill Creek Office has the largest case backlog with 354 cases awaiting a caseworker decision.
SC-PUB-004.narrative: Open cases with a new application, renewal or change report waiting at the reporting date (BR-PUB-013); showing the top 5 offices. The county backlog is 1,904 cases.

A.headline: Pine Hollow Office has the largest case backlog with 218 cases awaiting a caseworker decision.

SC-PUB-005.headline: Child Care Subsidy takes longest to decide this year at 20.6 business days.
SC-PUB-005.narrative: 89.0% of Child Care Subsidy decisions met the 30-day standard, versus 90.2% for Energy Assistance (19.8 days). Document holds are excluded (BR-PUB-002).

SC-PUB-006.headline: Riverside carries the largest case backlog with 658 cases, waiting 43.1 days on average.
SC-PUB-006.narrative: Backlog by service district for the districts you are entitled to see; the district row access policy RAP_DISTRICT applies to district-based personas.

A.headline: North carries the largest case backlog with 430 cases, waiting 24.8 days on average.

SC-PUB-007.headline: I can't decide applications — eligibility decisions are made by a caseworker.
SC-PUB-007.narrative: Agents act, humans decide: approving or denying an application is a caseworker decision that can be appealed (BR-PUB-028). I can show you processing time and the backlog for your office so you can prioritise the queue.

SC-PUB-008.headline: 311 resolution time averaged 2.78 days this year — within the target band.
SC-PUB-008.narrative: Monthly mean days from creation to closure over 9 months, excluding merged duplicates (BR-PUB-005).

SC-PUB-009.headline: Residents logged 1,988 311 service requests last month.
SC-PUB-009.narrative: Requests created by phone, mobile app, web and walk-in, excluding requests merged as duplicates (BR-PUB-005).

SC-PUB-010.headline: Potholes take longest to fix in Riverside: 5.10 days on average this year.
SC-PUB-010.narrative: "Fix a pothole" maps to pothole repair time — days from a pothole report to closure of the 311 request. North is fastest at 2.33 days; the 311 SLA for potholes is 5 days (BR-PUB-006).

A.headline: Potholes take longest to fix in Central: 2.36 days on average this year.

SC-PUB-011.headline: Commercial building permits took longest last quarter at 32.4 days.
SC-PUB-011.narrative: Calendar days from a complete submittal to the decision across 8 permit types, excluding over-the-counter permits issued the same day (BR-PUB-011). Sign permits were quickest at 16.4 days.

A.headline: Commercial building permits took longest last quarter at 36.1 days.

SC-PUB-012.headline: 311 SLA attainment moved +0.4 points from the first to the latest quarter this year.
SC-PUB-012.narrative: Share of closed requests resolved within their request type's SLA (BR-PUB-006) for each of the 3 quarters, excluding merged duplicates. County-wide attainment held steady even though the Q3 hauler change pulled Central's missed-trash SLA down.

SC-PUB-013.headline: That's a benefit payments question — the Payment Integrity Copilot answers it.
SC-PUB-013.narrative: I cover 311 service levels and permits. The Payment Integrity Copilot is certified on benefit payments, accuracy and improper payments.

SC-PUB-014.headline: The largest permit applicant this year declared $1,178,728 of construction.
SC-PUB-014.narrative: Applicant names are masked unless your persona is cleared for PII under MASK_PII (BR-PUB-023). Showing the top 5 applicants by declared valuation.

A.headline: The largest permit applicant this year declared $1,053,808 of construction.

D.headline: The largest permit applicant this year declared $1,178,728 of construction.

SC-PUB-015.headline: I can't dispatch crews — that is outside what this agent is allowed to do.
SC-PUB-015.narrative: Crews are scheduled by Public Works from the work order queue. Report the pothole through 311 so it is routed and tracked; I can show you pothole repair time in your district.

SC-PUB-016.headline: The improper payment rate is 2.56% year to date — within the target band.
SC-PUB-016.narrative: Improper dollars (over- and underpayments) as a share of dollars issued, excluding voided payments (BR-PUB-008, BR-PUB-009).

A.headline: The improper payment rate is 2.65% year to date — within the target band.

SC-PUB-017.headline: Income verification drives the most improper payment dollars this year: $81,225 (42.2% of the total).
SC-PUB-017.narrative: Total improper payment dollars are $192,344 across 4 error types, excluding voided payments (BR-PUB-008). Cash Assistance income-verification errors spiked in Q2.

SC-PUB-018.headline: 375 paying cases are flagged for program integrity review this year.
SC-PUB-018.narrative: Program Integrity is still in certification, so treat this figure as provisional. A flag is a review, not a finding of fraud (BR-PUB-010).

A.headline: You don’t have access to Program Integrity yet.

SC-PUB-019.headline: Across 5 programs, the median improper payment rate this year is 2.58%.
SC-PUB-019.narrative: The middle 80% of programs sit between 1.78% and 4.56%; the worst program reaches 5.85%.

SC-PUB-020.headline: I can't make fraud determinations about individuals.
SC-PUB-020.narrative: An integrity flag is a review, not a finding; only an investigator's decision, subject to appeal, can establish a program violation (BR-PUB-010). I can show aggregate integrity flag rates by district or program.

SC-PUB-021.headline: Public Works is furthest over budget this fiscal year at 17.0%.
SC-PUB-021.narrative: Actual versus adopted budget for FY2027 to date (July-September 2026, BR-PUB-015); positive is an overspend. Community Development is furthest under at -18.2%. The county as a whole is at -1.9%.

SC-PUB-022.headline: Procurement cycle time moved +5.5 days from the first to the latest quarter this year.
SC-PUB-022.narrative: Average days from requisition to purchase order for POs raised in each of the 3 quarters, excluding emergency purchases (BR-PUB-018). The e-procurement approval workflow that went live in May added steps to every requisition, and IT and software purchases also wait for a security review.

SC-PUB-023.headline: Transportation grants have the lowest drawdown at 24.1% of awarded dollars.
SC-PUB-023.narrative: Drawdown on active grants (BR-PUB-021) for the 5 lowest program areas; a grant is at risk when it trails its award period by more than 20 points (BR-PUB-022).

SC-PUB-024.headline: The workforce vacancy rate is 11.0% this fiscal year — within the target band.
SC-PUB-024.narrative: Unfilled authorised positions as a share of authorised positions for FY2027 to date (BR-PUB-015, BR-PUB-017). Eligibility Services vacancies are the main driver.

SC-PUB-025.headline: "The budget" can mean a few things — which one do you need?
SC-PUB-025.narrative: I can show budget variance by department, budget execution, or the workforce vacancy rate, for this fiscal year or FY2026.

SC-PUB-026.headline: In FY2026 every department finished within budget; Water Utility came closest at -2.8%.
SC-PUB-026.narrative: You named FY2026 (July 2025 - June 2026), so the current-fiscal-year default (BR-PUB-015) is not applied. Every department finished FY2026 within budget; Public Works' overspend is a FY2027 story.

SC-PUB-027.headline: I explain governance across the county data estate — I don't analyse service KPIs.
SC-PUB-027.narrative: Ask me what a glossary term or metric means, the certification status of a data product, or where governance gaps such as missing stewards, unmasked identifiers or open-data suppression sit. For KPI numbers, ask the domain agents.

SC-PUB-028.headline: I can't approve access requests — agents act, humans decide.
SC-PUB-028.narrative: Access to a data product is granted only by its owner or steward through the access workflow. I can show you the request status and who can approve it.
